newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel eases rules on forex, CPI deposits.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel eases rules on forex, CPI deposits.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Thursday it was further easing foreign currency regulations on individuals and banks.

The central bank said it had cancelled the one-month minimum term for a foreign currency-linked and inflation-linked deposits. From now on, forex-linked accounts can be for period of less than a month or held in a current account.

The Bank of Israel had been gradually reducing the minimum terms for linked deposits since 1988 as part of its programme of liberalising financial markets. Before 1998, forex-linked accounts were prohibted and until 1990 the minimum terms on a CPI-linked deposit was 30 months.
In addition, the central bank eased forex liquidity requirements for the banks by increasing the extent to which banks can diverge from a rule requiring forex assets and liabilities to be in balance.

Under the new rules, the extent of the divergence for all the banks in aggregate is doubled to $1.1 billion. For each bank, the new ceiling is 8.0 percent of assets or $40 million, whichever is bigger.

"The increase in the permitted divergence will enhance the banks' freedom of operations in making shekel/forex markets and is expected to contribute to the development of forex trading," the Bank of Israel said.
